sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Agent Behaviour Policies move to the Open Security Summit, as its first hosted project.
sections.para: A description of what an agent can do should not belong to the company that sells it, so the policy gets a home of its own: the Open Security Summit CIC, as the first project of a hosted-project programme. Hosting is not independence: a charter and an independent steering majority make that. RiskMandate stays a founding contributor. It is a proposal.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Seven points: why, where, the programme, independence, open, RiskMandate, phases.
sections.para: The policy needs a home that is not ours. The Open Security Summit, a UK CIC, will host it as the first of a hosted-project programme, not a new foundation. Hosting is not independence; a charter and an independent majority make it. The material is already open. RiskMandate is a founding contributor and implementer. It is a proposal, in four phases.

sections.label: Why it needs a home
sections.para: A format that the buyer, vendor, reviewer and insurer all write in has to be one none of them owns. That is why on 8 October RiskMandate's founders proposed it to OWASP. It was not the right fit for an OWASP project; the reason for finding a home has not changed, and there is a better one close to hand.

sections.label: The Open Security Summit
sections.line: The Open Security Summit: the host and the programme.
sections.para: The Open Security Summit has always been about developers and security working together, and since 2019 it has been a UK community interest company, which I direct. The CIC would be the legal host; a hosted-project programme sets the common rules; Agent Behaviour Policies is the first project, run by its own steering group and maintainers.

sections.label: Hosting is not independence
sections.para: Hosting separates the project from RiskMandate as an organisation, but I direct the CIC and co-founded RiskMandate, so independence must be designed: a public charter, a steering group with a majority independent of RiskMandate and The Cyber Boardroom, delegated technical direction, published rules, recorded conflicts, and no veto by funding. Until then, no claim of independent governance.

sections.label: Already open
sections.line: Already open: what hosting needs instead.
sections.para: The work is already CC BY 4.0 and Apache 2.0, so nothing needs to be made open again. Hosting needs an inventory of each asset, its licence, rights holder and provenance, with no blanket copyright assignment. In scope: the public method, schemas, templates, examples and contributed tools. Not automatically: product code, customer material, contracts or certification.

sections.label: RiskMandate's place
sections.para: RiskMandate becomes a founding contributor, sponsor, implementer and commercial provider, and says so; it is run today by The Cyber Boardroom, with a separate company expected. The project is usable without buying from RiskMandate, others can implement and contribute on the same rules, funding gives no veto, and RiskMandate is not the only implementation.

sections.label: Four phases
sections.line: Four phases, and the public description.
sections.para: Confirm the basis: the CIC's documents, the asset inventory and advice on conflicts. Establish the programme: approval, the first charter, independent members, funding. Publish and operate: infrastructure, rules and first releases. Review: whether outside contributors really influence decisions. The draft public description names the CIC as host and RiskMandate as founding contributor.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: It is a proposal, not an adopted charter or transfer. The governance is not yet independent. The CIC's documents have not been reviewed yet. It is not an OWASP project and not a separate registered foundation. Legal and accounting advice comes before any agreement between the companies.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: A voice memo and a hosting brief of 20 October 2026; Open Security Summit CIC at Companies House and the Open Security Summit's site; RiskMandate's proposal to OWASP; and the roadmap, commercial model and first customers articles.
